_README: Adjudicated QA verdicts, so a reviewed episode stays reviewed.
qa_check.py regenerates QA_CHECKLIST.md from scratch on every run, which means
its checkboxes cannot hold review state -- tick one and the next run erases it.
Without this file, every session re-discovers and re-investigates the same
already-adjudicated episodes. That is what kept the flagged count stuck at
14-16 while real work was being done.
Keys are episode slugs. Under each, a signature name maps to a verdict.
Signature names match the `signature` argument in qa_check.py's issue() calls:
wall-of-text, drift, content-loss, duplicates, backward-jump, truncated,
coverage, round-timestamps, weak-model, language, split-timestamp,
leaked-reasoning, repetition-loop, short-loop, missing-file
verdict: "benign" moves the issue out of the flagged list into a separate
'Reviewed, judged benign' section. Any other verdict (or no entry) leaves it
flagged. Always record a reason and a date -- a suppression with no rationale
is worse than no suppression.
Re-flag by deleting the entry. If an episode is reprocessed and its content
changes, delete its entries so the new output gets judged fresh.
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-28 -- the wall-of-text waivers on ep41/ep43/ep44/ep58, and ep44's
coverage waiver. All rested on one claim: 'the giant block carries a single speaker
label, so it is one real long monologue.' That is circular. A collapsed diarization
cluster produces exactly one label across the whole block, so the label count cannot
witness its own correctness. Reading those blocks found real co-host turns inside
them (ep58 'Devil's advocate sikit, YB'; ep43 'Kau rakyat jelata biasa?' answered by
'Saya rakyat jelita biasa lah'). The size trigger now lives in the separate
'oversized-block' signature, which does not consult the label count.
Waiving an issue needs evidence INDEPENDENT of the artefact under suspicion. Audio,
or dialogue content, or the roster -- not the label whose correctness is the question.

drift.reason: Isolated false phrase-lock, not mistiming. 10 of ep17's 11 matched samples sit within -21s; the single -958s outlier is a 124-char block whose head words score equally badly at the claimed and matched positions (2/10 both), so the match barely cleared MIN_MATCHING_WORDS and locked onto a coincidence. Block [7323s] independently maps to audio at 7441s (p10 7341, p90 7535) by 4-gram origin mapping, and the caption coverage map shows no near-zero run anywhere in the episode. See ENGINEERING_LOG.md 1.23.

Isolated false phrase-lock, same as ep17. Only 3 of 12 samples match at all because ep21's YouTube captions run at about half normal word density (8,182 caption words over 9,574s), which is also why check_caption_coverage.py reports it inconclusive. Two of the three matched samples are tight (-33s, -36s); the +976s outlier is contradicted by 4-gram origin mapping, which puts block [7574] at audio 7596-7669s (correctly positioned) and its neighbour [7832] at 7841s. See ENGINEERING_LOG.md 1.23.

oversized-block.reason: Genuine Rafizi monologue. TWO independent lines of evidence, neither of them the block's own label -- that was the circular error withdrawn on 2026-08-28. (1) Content: the 22.6-min block at [1:46:50] contains ZERO co-host markers across all of it. The four signatures present in every confirmed-mixed block are absent: no run-sheet clock reading ("2 jam 40 minit"), no segment hand-off, no question addressed to YB, no second-person address. It reads as sustained first-person self-defence, opening "naya lah semua menteri dituduh salah guna kuasa" and closing "ini doa akulah kan. Aku tak nak mati". (2) Acoustic: scripts/reattribute_blocks.py re-ran pyannote with an exact speaker count and left this block whole, on the same batch where it split ep45's 41-minute, ep44's 44-minute and ep43's 32-minute blocks into 153, 133 and 155 turns. The method demonstrably works on comparable episodes and declined here. Re-flag by deleting this entry if the episode is ever re-transcribed.
